name: Blueprint
reads_as: A technical drawing drafted live in white on deep cyanotype blue: a faint drafting grid, parts drawn in drafting order (centre lines, outlines with the sheet behind them, detail, hidden edges, hatching), dimensions with live amber figures, numbered balloons and a title block, all lettered in a single-stroke technical hand by one quiet glowing nib. Two registers: calm teaching sheets (a few large cards, connectors, revision clouds, a tracing overlay, general notes) for explaining, and dense detail sheets for how a thing is built or moves. Cyan for the part the narration names, amber for measures, coral or mint for a verdict. For engineers and technical staff: systems, architecture, failure modes, protocols, change control, how a thing is built.

ambient._note: the drafting grid is the fx blueprint background (one shader layer that follows the world), not DOM nodes: a per-dot ambient made a page of 96,163 nodes and checks 50 times slower (docs/research/2026-10-10-why-checks-are-slow.md)

characters._extras_note: what a background person is (D-100): people = the cast's rigs in muted clothes; silhouette = the grey bean; none = no crowd. A blueprint is about the system: people are rare and stay small. Change it here, never per lesson.

join_note: One sheet, one camera: pan and zoom across the drawing inside a topic (continue); a cut between topics; a wipe only at a section change, like turning to the next sheet.

fx._grain_note: D-100: grain is off or near-off by default; per-pixel noise reads as grit after H.264 on a 1080p MP4 (L-173). A lesson may set storyboard fx.grain to choose a film finish.
fx._background_why: 2026-10-16: cyanotype paper (mottled blues, fibres, fold creases, bleached edges) replaces the drafting grid, after Kshitij: the blueprint lost its wow next to lemo-opuscar's sheet; the engine's translucent part paper shows it through

pace._why: dark-field pack: thin white lines on deep blue measure low edge density by design, as dark-technical (D-112)
